page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn7i-c56g1.14xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance belonging to the ecs.gn7i family. It features 56 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 346.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 6.18 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it integrates a single NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPU with 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. It operates on the KVM hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps. No local storage is bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data highlights strong capabilities in specific compute and memory tasks. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 51,481.37 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 262.06 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. In LLM inference tests using smaller models, the hardware demonstrates top-tier performance, processing 9,738.91 tokens/sec for prompts and 457.19 tokens/sec for generation on a 135M model, as well as 2,464.01 tokens/sec for prompts and 89.85 tokens/sec for generation on a 7B model. Standard CPU and memory operations, such as stress-ng multi-core performance and Redis SET operations, perform in the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn7i-c56g1.14xlarge offers a dense allocation of dedicated Intel Xeon cores and Ampere GPU resources, making it a viable option for specialized acceleration without the overhead of multi-GPU configurations. However, the complete lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy applications. This instance is highly suited for workloads such as low-to-medium parameter LLM inference, database operations, parallel decompression tasks, and GPU-accelerated compute workloads.
